fields.apa_citation: Xie, H., Chen, Q., Nespoli, C., & Riso, T. (2022). Understanding the cognitive immersion of hospitality architecture in culture and nature: Cultural psychology and neuroscience views. Frontiers in Psychology, 13, 833819. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2022.833819
fields.main_conclusion: Using a single-case field study of the Amanfayun hotel in Hangzhou, the authors show that neuroaesthetic appreciation of hospitality architecture arises from the joint operation of sensory-motor, knowledge-meaning, and emotion-valuation systems (the aesthetic triad), which together explain how fused cultural and natural elements in architecture produce a balanced, immersive aesthetic experience.
fields.construct_pair: Cultural and natural immersion in hospitality architecture -> neuroaesthetic (sensory-motor, knowledge-meaning, emotion-valuation) appreciation
fields.stimulus_description: Participants (hotel guests) experienced the physical architecture, landscape, and interiors of the Amanfayun hotel in Hangzhou, China, a resort built to merge Buddhist-temple-adjacent natural surroundings with traditional Chinese design elements (sloping roofs, archways, natural materials, adjustable sunshades).
fields.methods_surface_summary: Single-case qualitative design: a team of six researchers conducted a 3-day field survey observing the hotel's architecture and landscape, supplemented by in-depth, unstructured interviews with three hotel guests of differing backgrounds; findings were interpreted thematically against three theory-derived propositions built on the aesthetic-triad framework (no statistical analysis).

notes.article_type: Borderline theoretical/empirical_qualitative: the paper develops a theory-driven framework (three propositions) and illustrates/supports it with a genuine single-case field survey plus three interviews, so it is coded as empirical_qualitative rather than purely theoretical.
notes.independent_variables: No manipulated or measured predictor variables in a formal design; the paper qualitatively documents architectural features (fluency, complexity, naturalistic patterns, familiarity, cultural context) rather than treating them as IVs.
notes.dependent_variables: No formally measured outcome variable; 'aesthetic appreciation/immersion' is discussed narratively rather than quantified.
notes.direction: Not applicable — this is a qualitative single-case/interview study with no quantitative IV-DV test of direction.
notes.sample_n: 3 interviewed hotel guests are the closest thing to a human 'sample' with reported data (Table 1); a separate team of 6 researchers conducted field observation but were not interview subjects/participants providing outcome data.
notes.stimulus_description: No controlled stimulus; participants experienced the real physical hotel environment during their stay/visit.
